narrative.overview:
Dravr reads like a quiet field notebook for training: one warm paper ground, one sage-forest green, and hairlines instead of shadows and of fill steps between panes. The product is dense and data-first, because athletes scan a thread, a plan and a set of numbers in short sessions, but it never looks busy: depth comes from a 1px ghost-border hairline and a half-step fill, and the single accent is saved for the one action that matters.

The same identity carries to the phone (iOS and Android) and to the editorial marketing site; the product tier adds visible hairlines, lifted pillar saturation and mandatory on-colour text pairings for high-density screens.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, green: primary is the fill, the ink and the link colour.
Hairlines lift, shadows float: the only shadow belongs to what hovers over the page.
Warm paper (#f7f6f2) as the one ground for rail, list and thread.
Tone is calm, premium, editorial; never glossy, never hype.
Every text/surface pairing is measured, not assumed (WCAG AA, 4.5:1).

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: primary is the only accent. Filled primary appears once per view; everything else green is the container tint or primary ink. There is no separate brand token.

rules.name: The Bound Ink Rule
rules.body: A hue may be a fill, tint, dot, rule or border. Text that sits on it takes the hue's bound on-*-container ink, never the hue itself.

rules.name: The No Dark-on-Dark Rule
rules.body: Any bg-primary or inline background at or below #234e40 takes text-on-primary. Dark-on-dark is a bug, not a style.

rules.name: The Alpha Rule
rules.body: Every --color-* holds a bare r g b triplet and Tailwind maps it as rgb(var(--color-x) / <alpha-value>). A bare var(--color-x) silently drops /NN modifiers.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case with no tracking. The DRAVR wordmark is the only letter-spaced label (headlines carry a slight -0.01em tightening, nothing more); uppercase tracked labels are retired.

rules.name: The Hairlines-Lift Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces are lifted by hairline and fill step, never by shadow. In dark, a black shadow is inert on a black ground.

rules.name: The Fill-Step-First Rule
rules.body: The fill step is the only channel that survives a screenshot or reduced transparency. Adjacent light tiers separate by at least 1.06:1; a raised surface over its canvas by at least 1.18:1.

dos: Do use primary for the one call to action per view and primary-container for tints (#e1eae5 / #234e40).
Do pair every fill with its mandatory on-colour (text-on-primary, bound on-*-container inks).
Do lift resting surfaces with a 1px ghost-border hairline and a fill step; reserve shadow-floating for what floats.
Do use sentence-case labels, 13px medium interface text and 15px reading text; set compared numbers in font-mono.
Do keep touch targets at 44×44px on coarse pointers and under lg, and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do route every colour through a token (alpha modifiers on token classes work), including the phone via useThemeColors().
donts: Don't pair a dark brand fill (bg-primary, or an inline background at or below #234e40) with text-on-surface; dark-on-dark is a bug.
Don't use a pillar hue as a button fill, a state, a progress bar or text; a state takes a feedback tone.
Don't use a stock Tailwind shade (text-amber-400, bg-red-500) or hard-code hex outside brand glyphs.
Don't add glow, a violet ring, a gradient on a resting surface, or backdrop blur on standard cards.
Don't use uppercase tracked labels; only the wordmark is tracked.
Don't let colour be the sole channel of meaning; pair it with an icon, label or position.
Don't raise a dark card with surface-container-lowest; it sinks below the canvas.
